title: Factorise a non-monic quadratic with a negative constant

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

student_prompt: Show your working and give your answer in factorised form.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: The signs are placed incorrectly. The constant is negative, so the bracket signs must be different.
Your brackets make -5x instead of +5x. Expand to check the middle term.

hint_ladder.title: What does the negative constant imply?
hint_ladder.prompt: A negative constant in a non-monic quadratic means the bracket constants have opposite signs. The position of those signs affects the middle term.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Choose first terms that multiply to the leading term, then test opposite-signed constants by expanding the cross-products.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: The signs may be opposite but still need the correct bracket positions, or the middle term flips direction.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For non-monic quadratics, expansion checking is the safest guide: first terms make ax^2, constants make c, and cross-products must combine to bx. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

common_errors: uses x in both first positions
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is building the correct bracket structure.
The stuck point is sign placement in a non-monic factorisation.

mark_scheme_notes: Award method credit for suitable brackets and full credit for (3x - 1)(x + 2).
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: sign reversal and insufficient expansion check.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, how will you check the signs in your brackets?
